Reinforcement learning, no magic

How I learned
to land
a craft

A story of software, physics and trial and error: from the Y axis to a craft that tries correct position, rotation and Earth gravity.

For software engineers who have never trained a neural network.

01 / The problem

What does landing mean in this game?

Touching the pad works if the craft arrives slowly, centered and almost vertical.

The simulator checks five conditions on contact: horizontal distance, X speed, Y speed, angle and rotation speed.

Final reward: +100 for landing, −100 for crashing.
|dx| ≤ 1,5 m

Inside the pad.

|vx| ≤ 0,7 m/s · |vy| ≤ 1 m/s

Soft contact.

|angle| ≤ 12° · |rotation| ≤ 0,35 rad/s

Stable craft.

Source: rocket.py, constants and RocketEnv.step()

02 / The environment

The simulator is the AI's API

Every 1/60 of a second, the AI sends an action and receives the new state, a reward and the flight's result.

observation→policy→action→physics→reward↺

Observation: x, y, vx, vy, angle, rotation, dx and dy.

Action: wait, engine, lateral thrusters or rotation.

# rocket.py, simplified
ay = cos(angle) * engine_accel * main_engine - gravity
vy += ay * DT
y  += vy * DT
reward = 100 if safe_landing else -100 if crash else -0.01

The network does not know these equations. It learns their consequences by trying actions.

Source: rocket.py, observation and physics

03 / Concepto

The AI learns a decision function

Given a state, which action makes more sense now?

In supervised learning we would give the correct action for thousands of states. Here we don't have it. The craft plays complete episodes and uses the rewards to tune its policy.

A policy is a function state → action probabilities.
High, centered, falling slow

It can wait.

Low, falling fast

It probably must fire the engine.

Tilted and spinning

It may need to correct before braking.

During training it tests actions; in evaluation it chooses the highest-scoring one.

Source: ppo_agent.py, select_action()

04 / Architecture

Eight numbers in, two answers out

8 inputs
position, speed,
angle, rotation, distance
→
64 neurons
tanh
learned combinations
→
64 neurons
tanh
more combinations
→
actor + critic
actions + state value

Actor: decides what to do. It has 2 outputs in Y, 6 in XY and 10 in XY with angle.

Critic: estimates whether the state looks promising. Returns a number.

Before entering, the eight values are divided by fixed scales to mix meters, velocities and radians.

Source: ppo_agent.py, PPOAgent.__init__() and forward()

05 / Real code

The architecture fits in five lines

Linear mixes numbers with trainable weights.

Tanh adds a curve: it allows non-linear decisions.

The actor's outputs are logits, scores that become probabilities.

# ppo_agent.py, abbreviated
self.body = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Linear(8, 64), nn.Tanh(),
    nn.Linear(64, 64), nn.Tanh()
)
self.actor  = nn.Linear(64, len(allowed_actions))
self.critic = nn.Linear(64, 1)
features = self.body(observations / scale)
return self.actor(features), self.critic(features)

The sizes and operations match the code; details were removed to read it on screen.

Source: ppo_agent.py, architecture and forward()

06 / Training

PPO adjusts the policy with recent flights

1

Play

The policy tests actions. It saves state, action, reward and probability.

2

Compare

The critic predicted how much each state was worth. The flight shows whether it went better or worse.

3

Adjust

PPO changes the probabilities and limits each change with clipping.

If an action went better than expected, PPO tends to repeat it in similar states. The limit prevents abrupt changes.

The code uses GAE to distribute credit between steps and entropy to maintain exploration.

Source: train_ppo.py, ppo_update()

07 / First phase

Y: learn to brake the fall

Two actions: wait or main engine.

The craft always starts at x = 0, at 9 m of altitude and with vy = −0.4 m/s. There is no lateral offset or rotation.

It learns the relationship between altitude, speed, gravity and ignition time.

89/100
landings in the last 100 training episodes
Firing too late ends in a crash; firing too early can brake too much or lengthen the flight.

Sources: rocket.py, reset_y_only(); Y metrics

08 / Second phase

XY: reach the pad

Lateral thrusters are added and the start moves in X.

The curriculum grows the initial error up to 3.5 m and the X speed up to ±0.5 m/s. The angle stays at zero.

The Y weights are copied and outputs for the new actions are added: an already learned skill is expanded.

100/100
landings in the last 100 training episodes
Y  = [wait, engine]
XY = [wait, engine,
      right, left,
      engine+right,
      engine+left]

Sources: ppo_agent.py, from_vertical_model(); train_ppo.py; XY metrics

09 / Third phase

XY + angle: stabilizing is also piloting

Now the craft can arrive tilted and spinning.

Four rotation actions are enabled. The curriculum grows up to ±0.45 rad of angle and ±0.30 rad/s of initial rotation.

The engine pushes in the craft's direction. When tilted, part of the thrust becomes X movement and vertical braking is lost.
100/100
landings in the last 100 training episodes
Engineering detail

In XY, angle and rotation were always zero. When transferring the model, their input weights are set to zero before learning this phase.

Sources: ppo_agent.py, from_xy_model(); train_ppo.py; metrics

10 / Learning signal

Intermediate rewards are hints

A +100 or −100 at the end says whether the flight worked, but not which of the hundreds of steps helped.

Training adds small hints for descending at a reasonable speed, moving closer in X and reducing tilt and rotation.

The real success condition is still the safe contact defined by the simulator.
# train_ppo.py, core idea
progress_x = abs(dx_before) - abs(dx_after)
reward_x = 8 * progress_x - 0.02 * speed_error**2

progress_angle = abs(angle_before) - abs(angle_after)
progress_spin  = abs(spin_before) - abs(spin_after)
reward_attitude = (
    8 * progress_angle + 2 * progress_spin
    - 0.03 * angle_after**2
    - 0.02 * spin_after**2
)

Source: train_ppo.py, the guidance_reward() functions

12 / The real world of play

The control handover discovered another problem

In play, the A key switches between human and AI.

A flight handed over to the AI at step 225 with the craft at about −93° and spinning at −1.67 rad/s. The original model did not correct that state and ended up crashing.

That state was outside the initial curriculum of ±0.45 rad and ±0.30 rad/s.
Usual training

The AI piloted from the start, with moderate tilt.

Human handover

The AI received the craft with accumulated tilt, speed and rotation.

Lesson

Working in one test does not imply recovering any state.

Sources: play.py; play log, step 225

13 / Learning from failures

The logs create new starting points

The model keeps its weights and practices recoveries near the handover that failed.

30% of episodes start near the log's state, with variations and a mirrored version. 70% keep normal flights to preserve what was learned.

The log's observations are used. The failed actions are not treated as correct answers.

97,3 %
landings in the 10,000 recovery training episodes
python3 train_ppo.py --mode xy-angle
  --init-policy model_xy_angle.pt
  --recovery-log flight.jsonl
  --recovery-step 225
  --recovery-ratio 0.3

Abbreviated command to show the idea.

Sources: train_ppo.py; recovery_curriculum.py; metrics

14 / Physics change

Earth: same control, different dynamics

Moon: 1.62 m/s²

Motor: 4.5 m/s² of acceleration.

Earth: 9.81 m/s²

Motor: ≈27.25 m/s², scaled in the same ratio.

Although the thrust/gravity relationship is kept, the velocities and the braking time change. The lunar model can fail in a mid-descent Earth handover.

The Earth run closed with 96 landings in its last 100 training episodes.

Mini experiment: instantaneous acceleration

ax 0.00m/s²
ay 2.88m/s²

Uses the simulator's real equations, without lateral thrusters. When tilted, vertical acceleration drops.

Sources: rocket.py, constants and physics; Earth metrics

15 / Generalization

The pad changes place

The observation includes dx = pad.x − craft.x.

That way the policy knows where the target is relative to the craft. In evaluation, --pad-range 3 places the pad between −3 and +3 m.

This experiment can place the pad farther than what was seen during training. Its result must be measured separately.

Reproducible test

python3 evaluate_ppo.py
  runs/ppo-xy-angle-earth/model.pt
  --episodes 100 --pad-range 3 --seed 42
A high metric with a fixed pad does not prove it finds new platforms.

Sources: rocket.py, observation(); evaluate_ppo.py, --pad-range

16 / Lessons

What this project taught

  • Reducing the problem made it possible to learn vertical braking first.
  • Transferring weights made it easier to add X and rotation.
  • The logs revealed states missing from usual training.
  • Earth gravity required training with the new physics.
  • The random pad needs a separate evaluation.

A neural network here is a tunable controller.

Its quality depends on the states it has practiced, the signals it receives and how it is measured afterwards.

Next experiment: measure separately normal landings, human recoveries and shifted platforms on Moon and Earth.
